title: In The Heights by Lin-Manuel Miranda and Quiara Alegría Hudes at New ...
transcript: I mean, what is there to say about this production other than “transfer it immediately”? In a firework of a revival, one that feels long overdue, In The Heights returns to New York with a joyous and urgent energy that demands to be experienced live. Lin-Manuel Miranda's vibrant and innovative score hits as hard as ever with its lyrical density, polyphonic melodies, and euphoric harmonic structures. I enjoyed the 2021 film adaptation, but sonically, it pales in comparison to hearing these orchestrations in person. The casting here is impeccable, with Aaron James McKenzie and Natalie Venetia Belcon being the vocal standouts for me. Matte Martinez is literally perfect as Usnavi — he carries the earnestness of a humble bodega owner and the swagger of a lifelong New Yorker with ease, dripped in charisma and humor. The most comedic performances, however, are from the scene-stealing Ishmael Gonzalez and Linedy Genao as Sonny and Daniela — they're giving a master class in making the most out of every moment. I was already familiar with the show prior to attending this production, which had already been open for a couple of weeks to universal acclaim, so I went in expecting to enjoy the material and the performances. I was not at all prepared for the level of choreography that they've pulled off over such a brief rehearsal period — it truly raises the already high bar for these so called “concert” productions. If they were to beef up some design elements and tailor them to a slightly more intimate theatre, this production would be ready for a Broadway run tomorrow. I think what makes this revival so successful is that they didn't overthink or overwork the material — it's still set in 2008, these meticulously crafted characters still feel familiar, and the bittersweet nature of their aspirations lives in conversation with the continued gentrification of New York. Every character in this musical has a clear motivation, and while the story illuminates how you have to lose something in order to gain something else, the pride that these characters have for their community is not going anywhere.
